c1-oba-0001: Obadiah has a warning for Edom. I take warnings seriously now. Peek at Obadiah 1:7.
c2-oba-0001: Edom should have stayed out of Judah's trouble. See Obadiah 1:12 and 14.
c2-num-0011: Israel asked to pass through Edom's land. Check Numbers 20:17 and 19.
c3-num-0005: Edom came out to block the way. Turn to Numbers 20:20 and 21.
c3-oba-0001: Jerusalem was in trouble, and Edom watched. Dig into Obadiah 1:2 and 11.
c3-oba-0002: God will judge Edom, but Jacob has a future. Find Obadiah 1:8 and 17.
c3-oba-0003: Edom hurt its own brother Jacob. Spend a minute in Obadiah 1:10 and 18.
c3-gen-0012: Rebekah heard about two nations. Edom later had kings. Read Genesis 25:23 and 36:33.
c1-nah-0001: Even in judgment, Nahum pauses to praise the LORD. Read Nahum 1:7.
c2-nah-0001: God promises Judah a better day is coming. See Nahum 1:13 and 15.
c2-nah-0002: Nahum compares two proud cities. Turn to Nahum 3:8 and 9.
c3-jon-0001: The king of Nineveh heard the warning and responded. Look at Jonah 3:6 and 10.
c3-nah-0001: Nahum pictures the fall of that great city. Check Nahum 1:8 and 2:6.
c3-nah-0002: The book ends with a word for Nineveh. Find Nahum 1:9 and 3:19.
c3-nah-0003: Nineveh is told to get ready for a fight. Dig into Nahum 2:1 and 3:14.
c3-jon-0002: God talks about His care for a great city. Read Jonah 3:10 and 4:11.
c1-zep-0001: Some in Judah mixed the LORD with other gods. Peek at Zephaniah 1:5.
c2-zep-0001: The LORD will search Jerusalem closely. See Zephaniah 1:12 and 13.
c2-zep-0002: Seek the LORD before His anger comes. Check Zephaniah 2:2 and 3.
c3-zep-0001: Zephaniah has sharp words for Jerusalem's leaders. Turn to Zephaniah 3:3 and 4.
c3-zep-0002: Some walked away from God, yet He still saves. Look at Zephaniah 1:6 and 3:17.
c3-zep-0003: God tells the faithful to wait for Him. Find Zephaniah 2:1 and 3:8.
c3-zep-0004: Zephaniah speaks of a city that felt too safe. See Zephaniah 2:15 and 3:1.
c3-zep-0005: Nineveh would be left empty, says the LORD. Check Zephaniah 1:4 and 2:14.
c1-phm-0001: Paul's letter is for Philemon, and for others too. Read Philemon 1:2.
c2-phm-0001: Paul thanks God for Philemon in his prayers. See Philemon 1:4 and 5.
c2-col-0004: Tychicus is coming, and Onesimus is coming too. Look at Colossians 4:7 and 9.
c3-phm-0001: Paul could command Philemon, but he won't. Turn to Philemon 1:8 and 14.
c3-phm-0002: Paul is sure Philemon will listen. Check Philemon 1:6 and 21.
c3-phm-0003: Onesimus was gone a while, and now he's back. See Philemon 1:15 and 18.
c3-phm-0004: Paul calls himself a prisoner of Christ Jesus. Read Philemon 1:1 and 13.
c3-phm-0005: Paul is sending Onesimus back to Philemon. Look at Philemon 1:4 and 12.
c1-2jn-0001: The Elder was full of joy about what he found. Peek at Second John 1:4.
c2-2jn-0001: The Elder writes about what love really looks like. See Second John 1:2 and 6.
c2-2jn-0002: Watch out for a visitor with a false message. Check Second John 1:10 and 11.
c3-2jn-0001: The Elder says to look to yourselves. Turn to Second John 1:8 and 11.
c3-2jn-0002: The greeting names the Lord Jesus Christ with care. Read Second John 1:3 and 9.
c3-2jn-0003: Some greetings are sweet, but some people deceive. Look at Second John 1:13 and 7.
c1-3jn-0001: The Elder wrote, but one man would not receive him. Peek at Third John 1:9.
c2-3jn-0001: That same man also treats the traveling brethren badly. See Third John 1:8 and 10.
c2-3jn-0002: Gaius has been kind to brethren and strangers. Check Third John 1:5 and 6.
c3-3jn-0001: A man is praised in this letter. Turn to Third John 1:11 and 12.
c3-3jn-0002: Traveling brethren set out, and the Elder is glad. Read Third John 1:4 and 7.
c3-3jn-0003: He has more to tell, just not like this. See Third John 1:11 and 13.
c2-exo-0022: At Sinai, God told Israel who they would be to Him. Peek at Exodus 19:6.
c2-2sa-0009: God makes a fatherly promise to David's house. See Second Samuel 7:14 and 15.
c3-jer-0013: God talks about a new promise, unlike the old one. Check Jeremiah 31:32 and 34.
c3-heb-0009: Hebrews looks back at Jeremiah's promise. Turn to Hebrews 8:7 and 8.
c3-2sa-0009: God reminds David that He has been with him. Read Second Samuel 7:9 and 10.
c3-gen-0013: God's promise to Noah still matters in Abram's day. See Genesis 9:12 and 15:18.
c3-gen-0014: God's covenant with Abram points to a big future. Check Genesis 9:15 and 17:4.
c3-gen-0015: The LORD appeared to Abram and called him closer. Turn to Genesis 15:7 and 17:1.
c3-gen-0016: Abram waited beside the sacrifice God had asked for. Find Genesis 9:10 and 15:11.
c3-gen-0017: Abram wondered about the land. God spoke again later. See Genesis 15:8 and 17:2.
